game_world: a dungeon crawler RPG (think Minecraft Dungeons)
title: Level Up: Variables are Your Player Stats
tagline: Time to code your first dungeon hero with health bars, damage counters, and epic loot stats!
scratch_bridge: Remember how you used those orange 'Data' blocks in Scratch to track your sprite's score or lives? Variables in Python do exactly the same job - they're storage boxes for your game data! Instead of dragging a 'set score to 0' block, you'll type player_health = 100.

concept.plain_english: Variables are like containers that hold information your game needs to remember - think player health, damage dealt, gold collected, or level number. Just like how your character sheet in an RPG tracks your stats, variables track all the numbers and text that make your game work. You can change what's inside a variable anytime (like losing health in battle), and you can use that stored info anywhere in your code (like displaying your health bar).
concept.why_it_matters: Without variables, your game characters couldn't have health, take damage, level up, or even have names!
concept.analogy: A variable is like a stat on your character sheet - it has a name (like 'Health') and a value (like 100), and that value can go up or down as you play.

code_example.title: hero_stats.py
code_example.code:
# Creating our dungeon hero!
player_name = "Sir Codesworth"
player_health = 100
player_attack = 25
gold_coins = 0

# Display the hero's stats with ASCII art
print("=" * 30)
print("    DUNGEON HERO CREATED!")
print("=" * 30)
print(f"Name: {player_name}")
print(f"Health: [{'█' * (player_health//10)}] {player_health}/100")
print(f"Attack: ⚔️  {player_attack}")
print(f"Gold: 💰 {gold_coins}")
print("=" * 30)
code_example.explanation: We just created our first dungeon hero! Line 2 stores the hero's name in a text variable (in Scratch, this was like the 'set name to Sir Codesworth' block). Lines 3-5 store numbers for health, attack power, and gold - just like 'set health to 100' blocks. The print statements show off our hero with a cool health bar made of block characters (█). The f-strings with {curly braces} let us insert our variable values right into the text - way cooler than Scratch's 'join' blocks!

challenge.title: Epic Hero Character Creator
challenge.game_context: Build a complete character creation system for your dungeon crawler RPG.
challenge.description: Create the ultimate hero setup system! Your code should create a hero with name, class (like 'Warrior' or 'Mage'), health, attack, defense, and starting gold. Then simulate finding a magic item that boosts one of their stats. Display everything with epic ASCII art including a visual health bar, stat comparison (before/after the magic item), and a victory celebration. Make it feel like a real RPG character screen!

===========================
Hero: Lightning Bolt Lucy
Class: Storm Mage ⚡
Health: [██████████] 100/100

encouragement: You just mastered the foundation of ALL games! With variables, you could start building Pokemon (HP, stats), Minecraft (block counts, coordinates), or even Fortnite (health, ammo, materials). Every epic game started with someone storing their first player_health = 100. You're officially a real game programmer now! 🎮
